ISSUE TITLE: Add CemaNeige degree-day snow routine coupled to GR4J
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters
GR4J is our flagship rainfall-runoff model, but it has no snow routine, so it systematically misses snowmelt-driven regimes (alpine Europe, Japan, Korea, the Himalayas, North America). The standard companion is **CemaNeige** (Valéry, Andréassian and Perrin, 2014, Journal of Hydrology), a two-parameter degree-day snow-accounting routine designed to be chained in front of GR4J; the pairing is what the reference R package airGR ships as GR4J-CemaNeige. Adding it turns a warm-climate model into a globally applicable one and directly widens the basins our calibration and UQ work can cover.

## What to build
- `CemaNeige` in `aquascope/models/` (or alongside GR4J): elevation-band degree-day snow accumulation and melt with the standard two free parameters (cold-content/weighting factor CTG and degree-day melt factor Kf).
- A coupling path so `GR4J` can accept CemaNeige-transformed precipitation (solid/liquid partition per band, melt added to liquid input), keeping the uncoupled GR4J API unchanged.
- Extend the existing auto-calibration (NSE/KGE/log-NSE) to optionally include the two snow parameters.

## Steps
1. Read the GR4J implementation and its calibration entry points.
2. Implement the routine per Valéry et al. (2014): fixed number of elevation bands, per-band temperature lapse, snowpack state, melt.
3. Unit tests: mass conservation (precip in = liquid out + pack change), no-snow regime reduces to identity, melt responds to temperature.
4. A short example or notebook cell on a snow-affected basin.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Coupled GR4J+CemaNeige runs end to end and calibrates
- [ ] Mass-balance and degenerate-case tests pass
- [ ] Docstrings cite Valéry et al. (2014)
- [ ] `pytest` and `ruff check` stay green

**Difficulty:** intermediate methodology (well-specified in the literature, mentorship available) · **Est:** 1-2 weekends. Comment to claim it!

ISSUE TITLE: Add CemaNeige degree-day snow routine coupled to GR4J
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters
GR4J is our flagship rainfall-runoff model, but it has no snow routine, so it systematically misses snowmelt-driven regimes (alpine Europe, Japan, Korea, the Himalayas, North America). The standard companion is **CemaNeige** (Valéry, Andréassian and Perrin, 2014, Journal of Hydrology), a two-parameter degree-day snow-accounting routine designed to be chained in front of GR4J; the pairing is what the reference R package airGR ships as GR4J-CemaNeige. Adding it turns a warm-climate model into a globally applicable one and directly widens the basins our calibration and UQ work can cover.

## What to build
- `CemaNeige` in `aquascope/models/` (or alongside GR4J): elevation-band degree-day snow accumulation and melt with the standard two free parameters (cold-content/weighting factor CTG and degree-day melt factor Kf).
- A coupling path so `GR4J` can accept CemaNeige-transformed precipitation (solid/liquid partition per band, melt added to liquid input), keeping the uncoupled GR4J API unchanged.
- Extend the existing auto-calibration (NSE/KGE/log-NSE) to optionally include the two snow parameters.

## Steps
1. Read the GR4J implementation and its calibration entry points.
2. Implement the routine per Valéry et al. (2014): fixed number of elevation bands, per-band temperature lapse, snowpack state, melt.
3. Unit tests: mass conservation (precip in = liquid out + pack change), no-snow regime reduces to identity, melt responds to temperature.
4. A short example or notebook cell on a snow-affected basin.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Coupled GR4J+CemaNeige runs end to end and calibrates
- [ ] Mass-balance and degenerate-case tests pass
- [ ] Docstrings cite Valéry et al. (2014)
- [ ] `pytest` and `ruff check` stay green

## Why this matters
GR4J is our flagship rainfall-runoff model, but it has no snow routine, so it systematically misses snowmelt-driven regimes (alpine Europe, Japan, Korea, the Himalayas, North America). Adding it turns a warm-climate model into a globally applicable one and directly widens the basins our calibration and UQ work can cover.

## What to build
- `CemaNeige` in `aquascope/models/` (or alongside GR4J): elevation-band degree-day snow accumulation and melt with the standard two free parameters (cold-content/weighting factor CTG and degree-day melt factor Kf).
- A coupling path so `GR4J` can accept CemaNeige-transformed precipitation (solid/liquid partition per band, melt added to liquid input), keeping the uncoupled GR4J API unchanged.
- Extend the existing auto-calibration (NSE/KGE/log-NSE) to optionally include the two snow parameters.

## Steps
1. Read the GR4J implementation and its calibration entry points.
2. Implement the routine per Valéry et al. (2014): fixed number of elevation bands, per-band temperature lapse, snowpack state, melt.
3. Unit tests: mass conservation (precip in = liquid out + pack change), no-snow regime reduces to identity, melt responds to temperature.
4. A short example or notebook cell on a snow-affected basin.

ISSUE TITLE: Add CemaNeige degree-day snow routine coupled to GR4J
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters
GR4J is our flagship rainfall-runoff model, but it has no snow routine, so it systematically misses snowmelt-driven regimes (alpine Europe, Japan, Korea, the Himalayas, North America). The standard companion is **CemaNeige** (Valéry, Andréassian and Perrin, 2014, Journal of Hydrology), a two-parameter degree-day snow-accounting routine designed to be chained in front of GR4J; the pairing is what the reference R package airGR ships as GR4J-CemaNeige. Adding it turns a warm-climate model into a globally applicable one and directly widens the basins our calibration and UQ work can cover.

## What to build
- `CemaNeige` in `aquascope/models/` (or alongside GR4J): elevation-band degree-day snow accumulation and melt with the standard two free parameters (cold-content/weighting factor CTG and degree-day melt factor Kf).
- A coupling path so `GR4J` can accept CemaNeige-transformed precipitation (solid/liquid partition per band, melt added to liquid input), keeping the uncoupled GR4J API unchanged.
- Extend the existing auto-calibration (NSE/KGE/log-NSE) to optionally include the two snow parameters.

## Steps
1. Read the GR4J implementation and its calibration entry points.
2. Implement the routine per Valéry et al. (2014): fixed number of elevation bands, per-band temperature lapse, snowpack state, melt.
3. Unit tests: mass conservation (precip in = liquid out + pack change), no-snow regime reduces to identity, melt responds to temperature.
4. A short example or notebook cell on a snow-affected basin.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Coupled GR4J+CemaNeige runs end to end and calibrates
- [ ] Mass-balance and degenerate-case tests pass
- [ ] Docstrings cite Valéry et al. (2014)
- [ ] `pytest` and `ruff check` stay green
